meta.title: Paatra: scholarships you can actually get
meta.description: Find the scholarships an Indian B.E./B.Tech student qualifies for, with the official rule quoted for every result. Your answers stay on your phone.

common.footnote: Eligibility is decided by the scheme. Always confirm on the official page before applying.

landing.headline: Which scholarships can you actually get?
landing.pitch: Pick your state and answer about 15 short questions. See every central, AICTE, state and private scheme you qualify for, and the exact rule behind each answer.
landing.startNote: About 3 minutes · no sign-up · answers stay on this phone
landing.trustQuotedBody: Word for word from the official page, with the link.
landing.trustCheckedBody: Each scheme shows when it was last verified. Nothing older than 90 days is shown.
landing.trustWhyBody: “Income ₹1 L over the ₹8 L limit”, not just a missing result.
landing.liveStates: State schemes go live one state at a time, starting with the {count} states and UTs whose rules we have confirmed: {names}.
landing.elsewhere: Elsewhere you still get central, AICTE and private schemes.

basics.title: About you
basics.intro: Skip anything you are unsure of. A skipped answer shows as “needs info”, never as a no.
basics.stateHint: The state on your domicile certificate, not where you study. It decides the category list below and your next few questions.
basics.incomeHint: All earning members, as on your income certificate.
basics.categoryHint: Choose your state first to see its category list.
basics.categoryNames: As on your caste or EWS certificate. SC: Scheduled Caste, ST: Scheduled Tribe, OBC: Other Backward Class, EWS: Economically Weaker Section.
basics.genderHint: Some schemes are for girls only.
basics.class12Hint: HSC is the Higher Secondary Certificate: your Class 12 board marks, as on your marksheet.
basics.institutionHint: Government-aided means a private college that gets government grants. A deemed university sets its own exams. Your college website says which.
basics.aicteHint: AICTE is the All India Council for Technical Education, which approves engineering courses. Most B.E./B.Tech courses are approved; your admission letter or college website says so.
basics.privacyNote: Saved on this phone only. We never ask for Aadhaar or documents.
basics.stateWithCount: {state} · {count, plural, =0 {state schemes coming soon} one {# state scheme} other {# state schemes}}
basics.chooseStateFirst: Choose your state to continue. Everything else can be skipped.

state.unlockIntro: Answer only the ones that apply to you.

state.stillPrivate: Private and CSR scholarships open to your state

results.mainHidden: The schemes that could fit you need one of the optional answers below first.
results.mainNone: No published scheme fits your answers yet. We add schemes every week.
results.mainIncome: Most schemes cap family income {range}. Yours is {yours}, so merit-based and private scholarships are your best chance.

results.noStateSchemesBody: We're checking them against the official portal now. Until then you see central, AICTE and private schemes. Come back in a few weeks: your answers stay saved on this phone.
results.answerFirstTitle: Answer {count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} to see what fits
results.answerFirstBody: You skipped some questions, so we can't decide {count, plural, one {# scheme} other {# schemes}} yet. That isn't a no. Each answer below settles at least one.
results.moreQuestions: Show {count, plural, one {# more question} other {# more questions}}
results.overlapNote: Government scholarships often can't be combined, so you may get only one of these state schemes. Check each official page and choose the one that pays most.

checking.note: This takes under a second. If the network is slow, your answers are already saved on this phone.
